interpretation: A single announcement email to existing local newsletter subscribers, introducing ClayRoom’s beginner pottery workshop, explaining the hands-on activity, and inviting readers to inspect the programme rather than asking them to book.
reader:
Selected audience (user-stated constraints): Local adults interested in trying a creative weekend activity; no employer or business buying process is established..
No further recipient situation is established. Compiled market context is research to check for applicability, not a replacement biography.
reader_segment: Local adults interested in trying a creative weekend activity; no employer or business buying process is established.
reader_profile_override: Local adults interested in trying a creative weekend activity; no employer or business buying process is established.
promise: ClayRoom offers beginners a practical introduction to hand building, with clay, tools and instructor guidance included, and the programme is available to inspect before deciding whether it appeals.
orientation: ClayRoom is a beginner pottery workshop where local adults can try hand building with the materials, tools and introductory instruction provided.
arc: Announce the workshop, make the activity concrete, set accurate expectations about the format, and invite the reader to inspect the programme.
sequence_rationale: One email is sufficient because the requested outcome is a straightforward announcement and the available evidence supports one compact proposition. The email should lead with what readers can try, clarify that this is hand building rather than a pottery-wheel session, mention collection after firing, and use the programme as a low-friction next step. No invented pain, failing status quo or urgency is needed.

emails.job: Help local subscribers understand what they can try at the beginner workshop and prompt them to inspect the programme.
emails.single_idea: ClayRoom’s beginner workshop lets readers try hand building with clay, tools and an instructor-led introduction provided; it is not a pottery-wheel session, and finished pieces are collected after firing.
emails.felt_need: I would like to try a creative weekend activity, but I want to know what I would actually be doing before I consider it.
emails.mechanism: The workshop supplies the clay and tools and begins with an instructor-led introduction to hand building. Readers make by hand rather than using a pottery wheel, then collect finished pieces after firing.
emails.belief_shift: Before: pottery workshop is only a vague activity idea. After: understands the specific hand-building format and can judge whether it sounds worth exploring.
must_not_say: Do not claim the workshop includes pottery-wheel use; it explicitly does not.
Do not invent dates, times, duration, location details, availability, class size, prices or booking terms.
Do not promise what object the reader will make or guarantee the quality of the finished piece.
Do not claim that no experience is required beyond describing the documented offer as a beginner workshop.
Do not invent testimonials, popularity, customer outcomes, therapeutic benefits, urgency or scarcity.
Do not present the programme CTA as a booking or purchase action.
emails.objection: I am not sure what a beginner pottery workshop would actually involve or whether it means using a pottery wheel.
emails.tone: Warm, clear and inviting, with matter-of-fact expectation setting.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether ClayRoom’s beginner hand-building workshop sounds like a weekend activity they want to explore.
emails.next_step_value: Inspect the programme with a clear understanding that the workshop covers instructor-led hand building with clay and tools, excludes a pottery-wheel session, and involves collecting finished pieces after firing.
emails.next_step_limit: Viewing the programme does not itself establish price, dates, availability or a confirmed place.
emails.subject_strategy: Signal a concrete beginner pottery activity and the opportunity to see what the workshop involves; avoid hype, urgency and unsupported claims of novelty.

voice_notes: Use the default plain, direct voice. Open briefly, address one reader, keep paragraphs short, and sign off as “- the team”.
